tasks.title: ui/candlestick_item.py — add the pure `capped_body_half_width` helper and cap `_draw_candles` at the pitch (S13/S14)
tasks.description: Add a module-level pure `capped_body_half_width(median_diff, base_half_width, px_per_sec, floor_px=4.0)` implementing `min(max(base_half_width, floor_px/2/px_per_sec), median_diff/2)`; `_draw_candles` calls it in place of the unconditional `min_w` clamp, and `set_data` gains an optional `pitch` used when `_width_override` is set.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 — AC-D6.4 (revised) / S13 — Given the pure helper `capped_body_half_width(median_diff, base_half_width, px_per_sec, floor_px=4.0)`, When evaluated over the three regimes, Then the rendered body width `2*w` satisfies `body <= pitch` in every regime: `body = max(0.65*pitch, F)` (gap > 0) when `pitch > F`; `body = F` (gap 0) at `pitch == F`; `body = pitch` when `pitch < F` (the floor yields to the pitch).

AC2 — AC-D7.1 (revised) — Given a rendered `CandlestickItem` at any bar density, Then the inter-bar gap `pitch - body >= 0` always and `> 0` whenever `pitch > F` (a zero gap is acceptable only at `pitch <= F`), and the wick remains a cosmetic 1-device-px line (the D6 wick clause is unchanged).

AC3 — S14 — Given `set_data(data, width=w, pitch=p)`, Then `_draw_candles` uses the supplied `pitch` for the cap when `_width_override` is set, otherwise computes `median_diff` from `data` exactly as today; the single-bar `w=0.25` fallback and the `0.325`/35%-gap intent are preserved.

tests.expected_result: body == max(0.65*pitch, 4.0) / == 4.0 / == pitch respectively; body <= pitch in all three regimes.

tasks.title: ESC-034 — the watchlist flash timer closes over a QTableWidgetItem that a column-layout rebuild has deleted
tasks.description: ESC-034: `RuntimeError: wrapped C/C++ object of type QTableWidgetItem has been deleted` at `ui/watchlist_panel.py:992`, inside the timeout lambda `timer.timeout.connect(lambda: item.setBackground(QBrush(QColor('#101218'))))`. `_flash` resolves the current item, highlights it, creates a single-shot QTimer parented to the PANEL and captures that item BY CLOSURE; `_rebuild_table` (reached via `_apply_columns` from the watchlist header menu — `_on_field_toggled`/`_move_field`) replaces EVERY cell item without touching `_flash_timers`, so an in-flight 400 ms timer fires against the freed C++ object. Fix by resolving the cell lazily at fire time (`_unflash(row, key)` doing `item = self._item(row, key); if item: item.setBackground(...)`) or by invalidating the pending flashes in `_rebuild_table` (as `clear()` already does) — NOT by swallowing the RuntimeError or by `shiboken6.isValid`, which silence the traceback while keeping a dangling intent. `remove_symbol` and `clear` are already timer-safe (verified) — `_rebuild_table` is the sole unsafe path; the fix must be robust to any item replacement.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 — ESC-034 (lifetime invariant) — Given a pending flash timer for a cell, When the cell's item is replaced by a column-layout rebuild (`_apply_columns`/`_on_field_toggled`/`_move_field`) or the row/table is cleared, Then the timer firing must not touch a deleted QTableWidgetItem: no unhandled exception is raised, and the live cell ends at the default background `#101218` (or the cell is gone and the reset is a no-op).

AC2 — ESC-034 (not a mask) — Given the fix, Then the pending flash is either invalidated when the items are replaced or resolved against the CURRENT cell at fire time, and no exception-swallowing shim is introduced around the flash callback (no `try/except RuntimeError`, no `shiboken6.isValid` guard) — the reset must not depend on catching a deleted-object error.

AC3 — ESC-034 (the already-safe paths stay safe) — Given the fix, When `remove_symbol` (first/middle/last row) or `clear()` runs, Then the removed row's timers are still stopped/re-indexed (`_flash_timers` keys remain exactly the live `(row, key)` set) and an uninterrupted flash still resets its cell to the default background after ~400 ms.

tasks.title: ESC-036 — D27.9 aggregator priming asks IBKR for `bar_size='5 secs'` with `duration='7200 S'` (error 321: invalid duration)
tasks.description: ESC-036: `ui/ticker_session.py::prime_aggregator` hardcodes `bar_size='5 secs'` and builds `duration=f'{prime_s} S'` with `prime_s = min(span_s, _PRIME_MAX_SPAN_S)` where `_PRIME_MAX_SPAN_S = 7200`. IBKR caps the duration for '5 secs' bars at 3600 S, so the '4 hours'/'1 day' timeframes (span_s > 7200) request exactly `duration='7200 S'` -> TWS error 321 'Historical data requested duration is invalid' (verbatim log: 'Aggregator priming request 144 failed [321]'), and `on_historical_error` fails open, leaving the aggregator UNPRIMED and the warning emitted on every load. Fix the request to a combination IBKR accepts: clamp the 5-sec priming span into `[60 S, 3600 S]`. Because the clamp can return 5-sec bars from BEFORE the current period's start, the replay must not fabricate a partial previous-period candle. `tests/test_d27_aggregator_priming.py::test_d27_9_prime_span_bounded` currently ASSERTS `duration == '7200 S'` — it enshrines the bug and must be CORRECTED (not weakened). NOTE (flagged, not decided here): 5-sec bars cannot cover a 4h (14400 s) or daily (86400 s) forming period at all, so whether those timeframes should prime with a coarser bar size (e.g. '1 min') or seed from the historical partial bar is a separate requirements question — see `docs/tasks/task_manager_notes.md`. D43/ESC-036 (second clause, decided 2026-10-16): this task delivers the FINE-timeframe branch only (`1 min`/`5 mins`/`15 mins`/`1 hour` -> `bar_size='5 secs'`, duration in `[60 S, 3600 S]`). The COARSE-timeframe branch (`4 hours`/`1 day` -> `bar_size='1 min'`, duration in `[60 S, 1 D]`) is delivered by the FOLLOW-UP task `P2-T35`, which supersedes D27.9's 'trailing 5-second history' wording; this task's AC1/AC3/T11/T31 no longer assert any 4h/1d request shape.

tasks.title: ESC-043 — scope the portfolio render to the live account and converge the `positions` table on the live session (the `HELD`/`H` rows)
tasks.description: ESC-043: the portfolio panel shows `HELD` and `H` rows. A read-only dump of the production DB (`config/paths.py::get_db_path()`) proves both are PERSISTED rows, not live updates (row 7 = HELD|DU123|999|stock|10.0|40.0 matches `tests/test_d27_account_subs.py::test_d27_6_positions_populate_panel` arg-for-arg; row 13 = H|DU1|1|stock is an ad-hoc probe write). They reached the DB because `tests/conftest.py` is hermetic for pytest but a NON-pytest offscreen probe with `DB_PATH` unset writes the user-space DB, and they were then RENDERED because `MainWindow._on_position_end` loads the WHOLE `positions` table with no account or qty filter (`ActivePortfolioPanel.set_positions` -> `_render_table`). Fix by scoping to the LIVE account: `_on_position_end` renders only rows whose `account` is one of the accounts of the current account-summary subscription, removes foreign-account rows from the `positions` table so the owner's existing junk rows (and any future ones) are addressed rather than ignored, and skips the prune when the live account set is not yet known. The live `position_update` path must likewise not persist/render a foreign-account update. The parallel task P2-T32 closes the isolation hole so a non-hermetic process cannot open the user-space DB at all. NOT IN SCOPE (a product call, flagged for the owner, not decided here): whether flat (`qty == 0`) live rows such as the six SPXW legs should also be hidden.

tasks.title: D43/ESC-036 — coarse-timeframe aggregator priming: `4 hours`/`1 day` must prime with `bar_size='1 min'` and a duration in `[60 S, 1 D]`
tasks.description: D43.1 (ESC-036 second clause, decided 2026-10-16): D27.9's 'trailing 5-second history' is unsatisfiable for the coarse timeframes — `4 hours` (period 14400 s) and `1 day` (86400 s) exceed IBKR's `3600 S` ceiling for `5 secs` bars, so `prime_aggregator` currently issues a `5 secs` request (clamped to `3600 S` by P2-T30), covering only the last hour of the forming period. Fix: select `bar_size` from the elapsed forming-period span — `5 secs` when the span <= 3600 S (the fine timeframes, P2-T30's branch, unchanged) and `1 min` when the span exceeds 3600 S (`4 hours`/`1 day`) — and clamp `duration` into the selected bar size's IBKR-accepted range (`[60 S, 1 D]` for `1 min`). This keeps a partial current-period seed and meets the revised `AC-D27.9` on every selectable timeframe.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 — AC-D27.9 (revised 2026-10-16 by D43/ESC-036) — coarse-timeframe branch — Given a fresh chart load mid-period on `4 hours` or `1 day`, When `prime_aggregator` issues its priming request, Then the request uses `bar_size='1 min'` (never `5 secs`) with a `duration` equal to the elapsed forming-period span clamped into `[60 S, 1 D]` (a 4h span is up to 14400 S and a daily span up to 86399 S, both inside `1 D`); and the fine timeframes (`1 min`/`5 mins`/`15 mins`/`1 hour`) continue to issue `bar_size='5 secs'` with a duration in `[60 S, 3600 S]` (P2-T30's branch, unchanged). No load issues a bar-size/duration combination IBKR rejects.

AC2 — D43 correction record (the enshrining test is corrected, not weakened) — Given `tests/test_d27_aggregator_priming.py` still carries the superseded wording (its module docstring says 'trailing 5-sec history'), When the coarse branch lands, Then `test_d27_9_prime_span_bounded` asserts the accepted coarse combination for a '1 day' load (`bar_size='1 min'`, duration inside `[60 S, 1 D]`) and the module docstring no longer states the superseded 'trailing 5-sec history'; the whole file is green.

AC3 — AC-D27.9 (no fabricated candle from the 1-min prime) — Given the `1 min` priming bars can include a bar whose ts precedes the current period's start (the `[60 S, 1 D]` floor at a coarse period boundary), When they are replayed into the aggregator, Then the aggregator's forming candle is the CURRENT period's and no completed previous-period candle is emitted from the primed bars; the existing fail-open-on-error / 15 s-backstop / replay-guard / live-feed-attaches-after-prime behaviour is unchanged.

tasks.description: ESC-053 (routed to REQUIREMENTS; the owner decision is now recorded here and in docs/tasks/task_manager_notes.md). The earlier 'NOT IN SCOPE (a product call)' note on P2-T31 is therefore SUPERSEDED, and the portfolio panel must hide zero-quantity positions from the render. The panel's position list and its rendered rows must remain index-aligned so the existing selection contract (`_on_selection_changed` -> `self._positions[row]` -> `_selected_position`) is preserved. tasks.title: ESC-054 — a real account's `position_update` arriving before its own `account_summary` callback must not be silently dropped (and must be recoverable once the summary completes)
tasks.description: ESC-054: `_on_position_update`'s foreign-account early-return is gated on `_live_accounts` being non-empty, but that set is AUTHORITATIVE only once the account-summary stream has COMPLETED (`_on_account_summary_end`). In the window between the first `account_summary` callback and `accountSummaryEnd`, a REAL second account's `position_update` is dropped — neither persisted nor rendered — and is unrecoverable for the session, because `_on_position_end` loads only from the `positions` table (reviewer probe: the row is absent before AND after the summary completes). Gate the early-return on completion as well (`self._live_accounts and self._account_summary_complete and account not in self._live_accounts`) so a pre-summary update is persisted (and rendered, still scoped to the accounts known so far) rather than discarded, and the panel converges on the complete live set once the stream completes. The completed-set gate ESC-043/ESC-052 established must remain intact (a foreign update AFTER completion is still dropped). Impact is nil for the single-account owner; real for multi-account users.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 — ESC-054 (a pre-completion update for a not-yet-summarised real account is not discarded) — Given the account-summary subscription is IN PROGRESS (at least one `account_summary` callback has arrived for account A, but `accountSummaryEnd` has NOT), When a `position_update` arrives for a real account B that is not yet in the partial live-account set, Then it IS persisted to the `positions` table (a row exists for B) and rendered, rather than silently dropped — a partial set scopes the render only, it never discards a real account's data.

AC2 — ESC-054 (the outcome is recoverable once the summary completes) — Given such a pre-completion update for account B, When the account-summary stream subsequently completes with the full set {A, B} (`_on_account_summary_end`) and `_on_position_end` runs, Then B's persisted row still exists in the `positions` table and is rendered — the panel converges on the complete live set and no real account's holding is missing for the session.

AC3 — ESC-043/ESC-052 preserved (the completed-set gate is not reverted) — Given the account-summary stream has COMPLETED and the live set is {A}, When a `position_update` arrives for an account outside that completed set, Then it is still neither persisted nor rendered (no `positions` row and no panel row) — the safety gate a reworker could otherwise revert remains in force.
